findings.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance
findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike Intelligence reported that an unattributed threat actor used the open-source agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX in intrusions against South Korean financial organizations, with activity running from late September to early October 2026 and resulting in data exfiltration. CrowdStrike assessed the framework lowers the skill barrier for complex intrusions.

findings.title: ARTEX AI Pentesting Tool Used in Data Theft Attacks on South Korean Financial Firms
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported CrowdStrike's findings that ARTEX was used in data-theft attacks on South Korean financial firms, with activity active from late September to early October 2026. The coverage summarized the framework's role in automating reconnaissance and follow-on actions.

findings.title: Storm-0940 Uses ARTEX Agentic AI in ConnectWise Supply Chain Compromise
findings.summary_md: Microsoft reported that the China-state-aligned actor Storm-0940 used ARTEX as early as September 2026 to automate attacks against hundreds of organizations across multiple sectors, including a ConnectWise supply-chain compromise. The post described intrusions progressing to privileged cloud access in under three hours.

findings.title: ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
findings.summary_md: Wiz Research identified activity using tooling associated with ARTEX throughout October 2026 against multiple IT and software vendors. The activity focused on ConnectWise ScreenConnect and credential harvesting against vendor environments.

findings.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant reported that threat actors have operated ARTEX and other multi-agent pentesting platforms in intrusions since late August 2026. Observed activity included large-scale Active Directory reconnaissance, Kerberoasting, and DCSync against victim domains.

findings.title: ARTEX: Agentic Asbestos
findings.summary_md: Censys identified 1,465 hosts running exposed ARTEX consoles as of November 4, 2026, with 155 hosts running at least one other threat-management tool. The finding highlighted how widely the framework's management consoles are left reachable on the internet.

findings.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
findings.summary_md: TechCrunch reported that security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the ARTEX penetration-testing tool exposed to the internet, allowing open access to the tooling. The coverage cited Censys data showing ARTEX instances publicly reachable.

findings.title: Beyond ARTEX: 45 AI Pentesting Tools and How to Find Them
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian cataloged roughly 45 agentic attack frameworks beyond ARTEX, documenting how they automate reconnaissance through post-exploitation. The post emphasized exposed management interfaces and leaked secrets as common enabling factors.

findings.title: Cairn, ARTEX and PentAGI: Hunting Exposed AI Harnesses
findings.summary_md: RST Cloud published hunting guidance for exposed AI harnesses including Cairn, ARTEX, and PentAGI. The post focused on detection and network-level identification of these frameworks' consoles.

findings.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
findings.summary_md: Palo Alto Unit 42 analyzed ARTEX and other AI-powered red-teaming tools, describing their use in real intrusions and defender detection approaches. The post framed these frameworks as a speed and scale problem for defenders.

findings.title: Artex and the Rise of Agentic Exploitation: Hours, Not Days, to Privileged Access
findings.summary_md: Obsidian Security discussed the FBI flash alert and how ARTEX compresses intrusion timelines to hours rather than days. The post summarized defender takeaways from the alert.
